# Mars Gods Eye — Mission Viewer

> NASA Space Apps 2026 project (challenge: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map; team: Houston, We Have a Bug!). A 3D web viewer that replays a saved, simulated expedition of an astronaut, a rover and a drone over a 2 km crop of real NASA/USGS CTX terrain at Jezero crater, Mars. It shows the orbital terrain prior and the map updated by (simulated) observations, height uncertainty, slope, proposed and invalidated routes, replanning, resources, geology and historical environment references. Everything shown is a REPLAY of simulated data, not a live mission, and it is not certified for real operations.

## What is real and what is simulated

- Real (NASA/USGS): terrain heights from the Mars 2020 TRN CTX DTM mosaic (provisional 2 km crop, 20 m grid); the draped MRO CTX orthomosaic (NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS/USGS, via JPL Mars Trek); geologic units from USGS SIM 3464 (Jezero crater and Nili Planum, 1:75,000).
- Historical references, not live weather: Perseverance MEDA daily summaries at Jezero (a few sols) and the published MSL RAD surface dose rate at Gale (Hassler et al. 2014), used for an estimated crew dose.
- Simulated or synthetic: the mission, agent motion, resource budgets, observations, the corridor scarp, routes and points of interest (POIs are fictitious). Vertical exaggeration is visual only (2x by default).
- The browser never plans routes: it draws the routes and decisions recorded in the replay.

## How to read the viewer

- Mode label: top right, "REPLAY · SIMULATION" (never LIVE).
- Tabs: Exploration (agents, tasks, routes), Ground layers (geologic map and schematic cut-away), Atmos (MEDA and RAD references), Mission replay (event log).
- Terrain layers: Orbital map (prior), Updated map (prior plus observations by map version), Slope (orbital CTX, Horn 3x3, about 60 m of ground per value), Uncertainty (assumed one-sigma height error, set by hand in the demo).
- Agent dial (bottom right): oxygen, energy, time, route, atmosphere and dose gauges around a heading-up minimap.
- Cameras: Map, Astronaut, Rover, Drone, Base; V switches the followed agent between third and first person. In first person the HUD shows a compass, site bearings, resources, the route ahead with the next waypoint, and a minimap.
- Drone camera scan (R): redraws the existing orbital slope around the drone in display bands (< 8°, 8–15°, ≥ 15°). It is not a new observation and changes no data; the bands await science approval.
- Keyboard: Space play/pause, ←/→ ±5 s, Home restart, F follow the selected agent, G grab-to-drag map, Q/E rotate, V first person, R scan, B camera sway in first person.
- URL parameters: ?run=demo (default) or ?run=mock-vertical-001 (a run recorded from the ROS mock vertical); ?nointro=1 skips the intro video.

## Machine-readable data

- [Demo run manifest](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/demo/manifest.json): title, summary, disclaimer, provenance, terrain grid metadata, POIs, AI disclosure and file list.
- [Demo timeline](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/demo/timeline.json) and [routes](https://jorgefajardom-coder.github.io/NASA-GODS-EYE-/replay/demo/routes.json): mission states, agent poses, events and route decisions over simulated time.
- In the running page, `window.mge.state()` returns the current replay state as JSON (time, mission state, map version, agents with pose and resources, active route, camera and layer), and `window.mge.about` repeats what is real and what is simulated.

## AI use (required declaration)

- AI tools were used and are declared in [AI_USAGE.md](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/AI_USAGE.md) and [ai_usage.json](https://github.com/jorgefajardom-coder/NASA-GODS-EYE-/blob/main/docs/ai_usage.json), with the affected files.
- The intro video (Kling) and the astronaut portrait (ChatGPT) are AI-generated and carry a visible "AI-generated" watermark. The simulated replay fixture was generated with AI-assisted code; it is not observational data.
